Project costing inside WFM (0104, WFM_PROJECT_COSTING.md).
Core-module subscription flags (0067).
PricingEngine (docs/pricing-engine-architecture.md): the dynamic pricing product.

Separate, narrower opt-in that lets a quote line actually pull a live price from PricingEngine's PUBLISHED "default" Price Book (spec: "never a forced migration") -- a tenant can have the Pricing workcenter without this
The Next Experience program (owner doctrine 2026-08-19, bpmsquarecore §10): the 3-layer theme, engagement layer, and every future "2050" interaction change live behind THIS platform-admin-only flag.
The "Enterprise" theme (owner correction 2026-08-25: it shipped without a gate and surfaced directly in the demo tenant's own picker -- not the design.
The "Spectacular" theme (owner request 2026-09-19, from an Able Pro dashboard reference): nextgen's structure with a softer, bluer, rounder palette.

Coverage (owner decision 2026-08-26, from the "Orbit" proposal): the rule-based Team/Segment/Coverage org model, replacing flat territory/ sales_org picklists with computed rules -- also drives auto-ownership, product av

AI Report Builder ("talk to data", docs/ai-report-builder-architecture.md): natural-language questions compiled to the same validated query engine the v1 API uses, answered with a chart/table over live data.
Fence Configurator (docs/fence-configurator-architecture.md, Phase C): parametric takeoff + BOM, priced through the same engine standard_quotes already uses.

RFQ (0128, docs/rfq-architecture.md): request for quotation to suppliers when no cost or price can be found -- a standard object raised from quotes, deals, cases, inspections, work orders and fence projects, with the sup

Marketing platform M0 (docs/marketing-platform-architecture.md): lead scoring, the consent ledger's settings and the lead stages.
Process Design Studio (0152, docs/process-design-studio-architecture.md): a prospect or client describes how they work and gets a cited fit report, proposed changes and a plan.
Newsletter Studio (0141-0143, docs/newsletter-studio-architecture.md): multilingual newsletter designs, templates and versions, handed to the existing campaign send path.
Buying signals (0175-0179, docs/signals-architecture.md): "Who is in market", a ranked, explainable list of accounts built only from first-party events.

Forms and the Preference Centre (0170-0172, docs/shells/forms-shell.md): forms hosted on the tenant's own domain and embedded on its website, each submit recording consent and creating the contact and a lead.
Account-Based Marketing (0180-0182, docs/abm-architecture.md): programs, target accounts and buying groups as their own object.
Journeys (0165-0169, docs/shells/journeys-shell.md): automated follow-ups that start from an event and run over days.
WhatsApp marketing (0185-0188, docs/shells/whatsapp-shell.md): approved templates, a consent-gated send, an inbound webhook and a journey step.

Attribution (0190-0192, docs/shells/attribution-shell.md): "Revenue by campaign", the deals and revenue each campaign, newsletter, form, journey, WhatsApp template and event started or touched, by first touch, last touch

Marketing events (0195-0196, docs/shells/events-shell.md): webinars, shows, roadshows and site visits, registration through an existing Form, check-in by staff, a results panel and a follow-up journey for attendees or no

Webhooks library (docs/design/webhooks-library.md): one list where every webhook is created and kept -- Event webhooks (the change feed) and Call webhooks (fired by a Standard Quote award, a record button or a Coverage r
Assistant actions (docs/design/assistant-smarter.md, section 3): lets the AI assistant propose a new record as a confirm card.

Assistant web research (docs/design/assistant-smarter.md section 2): the dock may ask "Do you want me to search the web for this?" and, on a yes, run one isolated search on our key and answer with sources.

abm.plain: Choose the companies that matter, work each one as a team towards a stated goal, and see how many were reached, engaged, in a deal and won, counted by company instead of by lead.
rules: A company can be in several programs at once, each with its own tier, progress, owner and next step.
Progress is a status set by fixed rules from what really happened (a quote opened, a deal opened), and a person can override it; an override always needs a reason and shows who made it.
Buying stage is read from Buying signals and is never changed or re-scored here; there is no ABM score.
The target list is a snapshot taken from a target group or segment and never changes by itself.
A buying group names people and their role for one program; naming someone sends nothing and needs no consent.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns; until then there is no menu item and no card on any other screen.

accounts.plain: Your customers and the companies you deal with, with their contacts, history and documents in one place.
rules: An account can have several contacts, assets, quotes and cases attached to it.
Phone, email and tax numbers on accounts are stored encrypted.

administration.plain: The administration hub: workspace users, roles and the audit entry points.

ai_assistant.plain: An AI assistant inside the workspace for drafting and for answering questions about records.

ai_assistant_actions.plain: The assistant can propose a new account or contact as a card showing every field; nothing is created until the person presses the button on the card.
rules: The assistant never creates anything by itself: it shows a card with each field and its value, the person can edit any value, and the record is created only when they press the button on the card.

A required field that is empty is flagged on the card and the create is refused until it is filled; the assistant fills a field only with what the person said or what is on their open screen, and never guesses a value.

Similar records that already exist are listed on the card with a button to open them instead, before anything is created; if the list is different when the button is pressed, the person is asked to look again.

The record is made by the object's own create route on the person's own session, so the module, the Business Role, the checks on linked records, encryption of phone and email, the reference number and custom fields all apply exactly as in the New form.
Each card can be used once: pressing it twice, pressing it as another user, or pressing it in another workspace does nothing.
Change History shows the record as created "via assistant", and an assistant action row records the card, the final values (phone and email are not written in the clear) and the result.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin, and it needs the AI assistant and Nova; until then the assistant has no create tool and the confirm endpoint answers 403.

ai_assistant_web.plain: The assistant can search the web for facts about a company, but only after the person says yes to that exact search, and it answers with the sources it used.
rules: Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and only with the AI assistant; until then the assistant has no way to search and says so.
The assistant asks first with the search written out, and the person answers Yes or No; a Yes runs that one search and is used up by it, so there is no standing permission for a chat.

Only companies are researched: a person, an email address or a phone number is never searched, and the search may contain only words the person typed or the name of the open account or supplier, never data from the workspace.
What comes back is treated as data, never as instructions: after a web result the assistant can no longer open screens, query data or change anything for the rest of that question.
The answer carries a From the web label and links to its https sources; if nothing could be cited it says it could not verify anything.

Each search counts against the monthly AI allowance (the tokens plus a flat charge per search), is limited to one per question and 20 per person per day, and leaves an audit row once the database update has been applied.
A workspace can switch external calls off in its own policy, which keeps web research off whatever the platform flag says.

ai_reports.plain: Ask a question in plain words and get a chart or table over live data.

amc.plain: Yearly maintenance contracts with the equipment list, visit schedule and renewal dates.

assets.plain: The equipment your customers own or that you service, with its history of cases and visits.

business_roles.plain: Named roles that decide which modules and screens each person reaches, together with the employee master and business users.

buying_signals.plain: Shows which of your accounts look ready to buy, in plain stages (Quiet, Looking, Comparing, Deciding), with every point of the score named and sourced, one next step per account, and a before-and-after view of which accounts a campaign moved.
rules: The score is a fixed, explainable rubric built only from your own records: quotes, deals, cases, contracts, campaign and newsletter clicks. It is never guessed by AI and is the same every time you open it.
Older signals count for less and drop out after 60 days; no single source can push an account past its cap.
Stage and score can be used as audience fields in Segmentation, so a campaign can target accounts that are Comparing.
An account owner is told in the Nova inbox when an account moves up to Comparing or Deciding.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns; until then there is no menu item and nothing is calculated.

cases.plain: A repair or service job from intake to closed, with its status flow, inspection report, photos and quote.
rules: A case has an inspection report that can be sent to the customer before the quote.

change_history.plain: A record of who changed what and when on every object.

contacts.plain: The people at your customers, each linked to an account.
rules: A contact belongs to an account and can be chosen on a quote or a case.

coverage_model.plain: Rule-based teams and segments that decide who owns an account, which products are available and how records are routed to an ERP.

data_workbench.plain: Import, export and bulk update of records from spreadsheets, with a template per object.
rules: Update always works from a previous export, matched by record id, never by name.

db_export.plain: A full export of the workspace data for backup or migration.

dispatch.plain: Plan which technician goes where and when.

enterprise_theme.plain: An unreleased enterprise look for the workspace.

estimator.plain: Turn a few answers or an element schedule into a bill of materials, a cost build-up and a standard quote, using templates your admin sets up once.
rules: An estimate belongs to a template made of inputs, rates and rule lines.
Once an estimate has a quote, its numbers can no longer change.

fence_projects.plain: A parametric fence takeoff and bill of materials, priced through Standard Quotes. Specific to fencing contractors.

gmail_reply_threading.plain: Quotes sent as a real reply inside the customer's existing email thread, through the company's Gmail.

integration_middleware.plain: One place for everything about sync with your ERP: connect it, choose what goes out when a Standard Quote is awarded or rejected, check the field mapping against the ERP's own field list, watch every message in and out, and retry anything that failed.
rules: An awarded quote becomes a Quote in Dynamics 365 Sales (made Active, then marked Won) or a Project in Finance and Operations and Business Central; a rejected quote closes the Dynamics quote as lost and sends nothing to a project system, and says so.

Each outcome is on or off, automatic or manual; automatic sends only after the person's save has finished and can never fail or slow it, and a failure is recorded with what happened and the one thing to do, then retried safely from the Resync tab.

One BPMSquare quote is one ERP document: sending twice, or retrying after a failure halfway, continues from where it stopped and never creates a second one; the BPMSquare reference is written into the ERP document's name.
A customer must already be in the ERP (synced from it); the middleware never creates accounts there, and a quote for an unsynced customer fails with the fix instead.

Fence project and estimate data leave only as ticked; a Quote carries customer prices only, so bill of materials, project tasks and internal costs go to Project targets, and internal costs only when explicitly ticked.

The message monitor shows email, WhatsApp, webhook, connector and API traffic to admins only; bodies and phone numbers stay encrypted in lists, opening one is change-logged, and request bodies are kept (redacted, 30 days) only if payload capture is switched on.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin; until then there is no menu item, no logging and no dispatch, and a pending database update shows as "database update needed" instead of an error.

invoices.plain: Invoice from a quote or a work order, send it by email and record payment.
rules: BPMSquare is not an accounting system: invoices are handed over to the customer's own accounting software.

journeys.plain: Automated follow-ups that start from something that happened, such as a quote being sent, wait a few days, send a newsletter version and create a task for the owner.
rules: Every message checks the person's consent at the moment it is sent; no consent, no message, and the run log says why.
A person goes through a journey once; nobody is entered twice.
Messages wait for quiet hours and the weekly day off, and a person gets at most one journey email a day.
Promotional steps pause while the company has an open case that has dragged on or an overdue invoice.
A demo workspace never reaches a real customer; the email output setting applies exactly as for campaigns.
Turning a journey on that would enter more than 200 people asks for confirmation first.
Try it on one person shows the path and the reasons and sends nothing.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns; until then there is no menu item and no runner work.

leads.plain: Enquiries before they become a customer or a deal, including those that arrive from marketing campaigns.

marketing.plain: Email campaigns to segments of accounts, with unsubscribe links and interest links that turn replies into leads.

marketing_attribution.plain: See which campaigns, newsletters, forms, journeys, WhatsApp messages and events started or touched your deals and revenue, by first touch, last touch or an even split, with a plain note on what that can and cannot tell you.
rules: It only reads: it never changes a deal, a quote, an invoice or a person.
A touch is something a customer did or was sent (a click, a form, a registration, a message); each is taken from the activity already recorded and is never counted twice.

Started a deal means touches before the deal was created, shared by the model you choose; touched a deal means any touch in the 90 days before it closed or today, so touched figures overlap and must not be added up.
Revenue is the deal amount for won deals and the paid amount on its invoices; it is a guide to where to look, not proof that a campaign caused a sale.
The figures are recomputed every few hours and show when they were last updated.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns; until then there is no menu item and no work is done.

marketing_events.plain: Plan a webinar, show, roadshow or site visit, let people register through a form, check them in on the day, see how many came, and start a follow-up journey for those who came or those who did not.
rules: Registration happens through an existing form, so the person's consent is recorded exactly as the form says; an event never records consent by itself.
A person registers once per event; a second submission changes nothing and is not counted twice.
Staff check people in; an attended person stays attended, a no-show can still be marked attended, and a cancelled person can be registered again.
Registering, attending and not coming are recorded as activity so journeys and revenue reports can see them.
The follow-up only starts a journey you already built and turned on, once per person; it never sends anything by itself and the journey keeps every consent and quiet-hours rule.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns and Forms; until then there is no menu item and no form is linked to an event.

marketing_forms.plain: Put a contact form on the company website that records what the visitor agreed to, adds them as a contact and files a lead, and let every person change what they hear about from one page.
rules: The consent box is never ticked for the visitor; the exact words shown, the time and the form are kept with each answer.
A person who ticks the box is recorded as agreeing to the topics the form names; a person who does not tick it is not recorded as agreeing to anything.
An existing contact is found by email and is never changed by a form; a new visitor becomes a prospect account, a contact and a lead.
Spam is stopped by a hidden trap field, a minimum time to fill in, a limit per visitor and a size cap; no CAPTCHA is shown.
The raw answers are kept for 180 days and stored encrypted; only the contact, lead and consent records remain after that.
The preference page opens from a signed link in each email and every change is added to the consent history.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns; until then the public pages answer not found and there is no menu item.

marketing_scoring.plain: Scores each lead from what the person actually did, moves it through clear stages, and checks consent before anyone is contacted. Staff can record what a person told them, and bring a sheet of opt-ins in.
rules: Consent is required by default; an admin can relax it for a country, but not for India.
A score always shows the reasons behind it.
A person in sales can record that someone agreed or withdrew, with a required note on how it was obtained; answers are only ever added, never edited.
A sheet of opt-ins can be imported in the Data Workbench: each row needs its basis, is matched to an existing contact by email, and keeps the file name as evidence. It never creates contacts.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin; until then no screen or lead changes.

newsletter_studio.plain: Design a newsletter once in English, add languages on top with AI translation you review, keep it as a template, and hand it to a campaign so each person gets their own language. Delivery problems are recorded on the contact so sales can fix the address.
rules: English is written first for every newsletter; other languages are added on top and each translated block is marked until a person accepts it.
A language can be sent only when every block has been reviewed by a person.
The footer always carries the unsubscribe and preferences links and cannot be removed.
Sending checks consent for each person and follows the workspace's email output setting, so a demo workspace never reaches a real customer.
Clicks are tracked on signed links; opens are not tracked unless an admin turns that on.
When an email bounces or is marked as spam, the contact's email health shows it; an address that bounced for good or was reported as spam is never emailed again.

Sales can check an address, fix it, or mark it as checked with a reason; each of these is kept in the change history. Contacts with an email problem are listed under Contacts, "Email needs attention".
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin and needs Marketing campaigns; until then there is no menu item and no campaign page changes.

next_experience.plain: Nova, the unreleased Business OS experience layer.

outbound_email.plain: Send quotes, invoices and campaigns by email from the workspace.
rules: A demo workspace can only email one internal inbox, never a real customer.

partners.plain: The OEMs and vendors who refer work to you, linked to the jobs they send.

pipeline.plain: Deals on a board, stage by stage, with the quote lines attached and a won or lost outcome.
rules: The deal stages are set by the workspace admin.
A rule such as a manager must approve above an amount is not a setting today.

pricing_engine.plain: Dynamic pricing: price books, routing rules by customer or document type, margin guardrails and approvals.

pricing_engine_quotes.plain: Lets a quote line pull a live price from the published price book.

process_studio.plain: Describe how a business works and get a fit report against BPMSquare, proposed changes and a plan.
rules: A fit rating is only given with a named module, screen or setting behind it.
Effort is shown as Small, Medium or Large, never as a price.

products.plain: A product catalogue with prices and categories; a product can be a kit with a multi-level bill of materials and a cost roll-up.

purchasing.plain: Purchase orders to suppliers, receiving, and inventory records of the stock you hold.

quotations.plain: Repair, supply, technical, budgetary and installation offers with print, email and a WhatsApp link to the PDF.
rules: A quotation moves through a status flow that the workspace admin can change.
A quotation prints as a PDF with the company's branding and terms.

quote_lines_dw.plain: Bulk loading and editing of quote lines from a spreadsheet through the Data Workbench.

reports.plain: Analytics tiles and reports over live data, on a dashboard.

rfq.plain: Ask several suppliers for prices by email, receive their replies back inside BPMSquare, compare and award.
rules: Supplier replies are read from the email and filled into the request for a person to confirm.

sales_orders.plain: Sales orders made from an accepted quote or a won deal, with an order type per workspace, availability from stock and lead times, a PDF to send, and files.
rules: An order is made from an accepted standard quote, a won quotation or a won deal; the lines and prices are copied, never retyped.
Each order has a type; the type sets the numbering prefix, the pricing mode and the PDF design.
A draft can be changed freely; a confirmed order stays open only for notes, customer PO and files.
Sending the order to an ERP and checking it there are not part of this module yet.

spectacular_theme.plain: An unreleased alternative look for the workspace.

standard_quotes.plain: Quotes with lines, alternative options, templates, PDF and email, with a status from draft to accepted.
rules: A quote line can offer alternatives for the customer to choose from.
A standard quote can be created from an estimate or a fence project.
Quote lines can be priced from the pricing engine, a price list, or typed in.

suppliers.plain: Your vendors, with contacts and the products they supply.

technicians.plain: Your field people, their skills and their work orders.

webhooks_library.plain: One list where every webhook is created and kept: change-feed events pushed to a system, and calls fired by a quote award, a record button or a Coverage route, each with its own address, headers, payload and test.
rules: A webhook is an Event (the signed change feed, sent in batches) or a Call (one record sent when something fires it); the kind and, for a Call, the object (Accounts or Standard Quotes) are fixed after it is created.

The address must use https and a public host; a private or internal address, a redirect to one, and personal data or a list inside the address are refused, and an older http address kept from the ERP push does not fire until it is edited to https.
The signing secret and every header value are sealed and write-only: after saving they read back only as "set", and the secret can be regenerated but never shown again.

A Call sends the standard signed record or the admin's own JSON template with a closed list of tokens; personal data is left out unless allowed, cost and margin fields are never available, and a template that does not parse or uses an unknown token is refused with the token named.

Every call is a row in the message monitor with its request and response; a failed one is retried once after 2 seconds on a network error, 429 or 5xx, can be restarted, carries the same idempotency key on every attempt, and the webhook pauses itself after 15 failures in a row.

An awarded Standard Quote reaches a webhook only through the Links target, once: sending twice or restarting never fires it twice, and a rejected quote never leaves; a demo workspace records the call and sends nothing.
Deleting a webhook that a Link, a Coverage route or the Accounts button uses is refused and names where.
Switched on per workspace by a platform admin; until then there is no menu item and no route, and a pending database update shows as "database update needed" instead of an error.

wfm.plain: Workforce: attendance by phone or door tablet, shifts, sites with a geofence, roster, leave, overtime and a monthly summary.
rules: An employee cannot alter attendance data.
Overtime and attendance corrections are approved by a supervisor.
Shifts, sites and leave types are set up by the workspace admin.

wfm_projects.plain: Hours per project taken from attendance, for project costing, without money shown at the first level.

whatsapp_marketing.plain: Send an approved WhatsApp template message to a person who agreed to hear from you on WhatsApp, see what was sent and answered, and add a WhatsApp step to a journey.
rules: Nothing is sent to a person who has not agreed to WhatsApp for the template's topic, who withdrew, or who is marked do not contact; this is checked at the moment of sending and cannot be switched off.
Only templates marked approved can be sent, and a message outside 24 hours of the person's last reply can only be a template; a free-form reply is for a person on the record and never for a journey.
A reply of STOP (or the Arabic equivalent) withdraws the person's WhatsApp consent at once; START records it again.
A demo workspace never reaches a real number: a message goes to the test number set for the workspace, or is only logged.
The shell has no live WhatsApp provider yet; the default is a sandbox that logs what would be sent and calls nothing outside.
